context_scope: acute SCI pharmacology
exact_evidence_status: exact ATP-P2X7R agonist-receptor edge at pharmacologic level
evidence_summary: Rat impact SCI shows sustained extracellular ATP, ATP-evoked calcium injury, and OxATP or PPADS protection; independent SCI and spinal-slice studies support ATP-gated P2X7 pharmacology.
limitations: OxATP, PPADS, and BBG have selectivity limits; pharmacology does not establish purified binding or exclude contributions from other ATP receptors.

context_scope: ATP-evoked calcium and P2X agonist challenge
exact_evidence_status: exact ATP-P2X4R agonist-receptor edge at pharmacologic level
evidence_summary: SCI ATP-evoked calcium and P2X4-associated pain signaling are supported by an independent SCI study showing excess ATP and P2X4 inhibition reduce neuropathic pain.
limitations: Evidence is pharmacologic rather than purified binding; P2X4 selectivity and ATP receptor-family contributions remain bounded.

context_scope: recombinant ligand and antagonist assays
exact_evidence_status: exact CXCL10-CXCR3 chemokine-GPCR edge; receptor-proximal function
evidence_summary: Recombinant CXCL10 and CXCR3 antagonist AMD487 altered glial activation and inflammatory pain after spinal ischemia-reperfusion; independent CCI studies reproduce CXCL10-CXCR3 pharmacology with AMG487 or anti-CXCL10.
limitations: No purified binding; most SCI corroboration is ischemia-reperfusion or CCI rather than contusion; antagonist specificity remains a limitation.

context_scope: ligand administration and CXCR2 inhibition
exact_evidence_status: exact CXCL3-CXCR2 chemokine-GPCR edge; receptor-proximal function
evidence_summary: Mouse traumatic SCI CXCL3 administration and CXCR2 inhibition link the pair to macrophage-fibroblast scar signaling; independent CINC-3/CXCL3 receptor pharmacology shows CXCR2-dependent chemotaxis and calcium responses.
limitations: No purified binding; CXCR2 inhibitor specificity and administration route limit causal interpretation; scar output remains downstream of the receptor edge.

context_scope: BK exposure and B2R antagonist/microglial GDNF assays
exact_evidence_status: exact bradykinin-BDKRB2 edge at receptor-proximal pharmacologic level
evidence_summary: Neonatal mouse spinal preparation and microglia assays support bradykinin/B2R effects; independent rat spinal ischemia and spinal-slice antagonist studies support B2R-dependent bradykinin responses.
limitations: Primary spinal study is neonatal and not adult lesion-core tissue; receptor assignment is pharmacologic and no purified bradykinin-B2R binding or endogenous lesion release was shown.

context_scope: cAMP, RhoA, and chemotaxis assays
exact_evidence_status: exact UDP-GlcNAc-P2Y14 molecular edge; no SCI-context claim
evidence_summary: Recombinant P2Y14 and differentiated HL60 or neutrophil studies show UDP-N-acetylglucosamine activation of Gi/Rho and chemotaxis, with independent pharmacology and newer structure-function work reproducing receptor-specific activity.
limitations: High confidence is molecular only; no endogenous SCI release or lesion-context evidence; efficacy and partial agonism vary by cell state and assay.

context_scope: cAMP, RhoA, and chemotaxis assays
exact_evidence_status: exact UDP-galactose-P2Y14 molecular edge; no SCI-context claim
evidence_summary: Recombinant P2Y14 and differentiated HL60 or neutrophil studies show UDP-galactose-associated Gi/Rho signaling, independently reproduced by receptor-structure/function and cell-death release studies.
limitations: High confidence is molecular only; no endogenous SCI release; receptor efficacy is cell-state-dependent and the ligand can show partial activity in native cells.

context_scope: cAMP, RhoA, and neutrophil assays
exact_evidence_status: exact UDP-glucuronic-acid-P2Y14 molecular edge; assay-dependent efficacy
evidence_summary: Recombinant P2Y14 and differentiated HL60 assays support UDP-glucuronic acid receptor activity, with independent human neutrophil and newer structure-function studies testing the same ligand-receptor edge.
limitations: High confidence is molecular only; no SCI release evidence; activity is weaker or partial in native neutrophils and depends on cell state.

context_scope: EP4 agonist and inflammatory cytokine assays
cell_type_context: primary spinal cord cultures and microglial inflammatory context
exact_evidence_status: exact PGE2-EP4 prostanoid-GPCR edge; receptor branch separated from EP2
evidence_summary: PGE2-EP4 activity is supported in primary spinal cultures and by independent recombinant EP4 binding, desensitization, structural, and myeloid functional studies.
limitations: High confidence is the molecular/receptor branch; EP2 and other prostanoid receptors remain separate; the primary SCI evidence is spinal culture or neuroinflammation rather than contusion.

context_scope: TLR4 blockade/knockdown, cytokine and MAPK/NFkB readouts
exact_evidence_status: exact resistin-TLR4/MD2 complex edge; receptor-proximal signaling
evidence_summary: Primary human or mouse TLR4 reconstitution and blockade studies support resistin-TLR4/MD2 inflammatory signaling; independent central binding and macrophage studies reproduce TLR4-dependent resistin effects.
limitations: High confidence is a molecular complex edge, not SCI evidence; TLR4/MD2 context and tissue-specific resistin biology remain limitations.

context_scope: FLRT3 oligomerization, interface-mutant, and cell-adhesion assays
exact_evidence_status: exact FLRT3-FLRT3 homophilic adhesion edge; not a downstream signaling claim
evidence_summary: FLRT3 LRR interface mutants and full-length aggregation support FLRT3-FLRT3 homophilic adhesion, with independent developmental studies showing FLRT3-family homophilic contact localization.
limitations: This promotes a molecular adhesion edge only; some studies find no soluble or trans homophilic binding, and heterophilic FLRT3-ADGRL3/UNC5 edges must remain separate from adhesion and SCI function.

context_scope: LEAP2 administration, ghrelin challenge, and GHSR-null specificity
exact_evidence_status: exact LEAP2-GHSR antagonist/inverse-agonist molecular edge
evidence_summary: GHSR-null specificity and ghrelin-challenge experiments establish LEAP2 antagonism; independent discovery and fluorescent-LEAP2 studies show GHSR binding, antagonism, and inverse agonism.
limitations: High confidence is molecular/pharmacologic; no SCI evidence and the evidence is not a purified structural binding assay.

context_scope: recombinant SAA1-TLR4/MD2 binding and NFkB assays
cell_type_context: heterologous receptor and inflammatory cell systems
exact_evidence_status: exact SAA1-TLR4/MD2 complex edge with direct binding and independent microglia confirmation
evidence_summary: SPR/co-IP and TLR4 or MD2 perturbation support direct SAA1-TLR4/MD2 engagement; an independent 2026 primary microglia study confirms biochemical interaction and TLR4/MD2-dependent inflammatory activation.
limitations: High confidence is the TLR4/MD2 complex edge; no SCI model; SAA1 receptor usage is context-dependent and the microglia study uses pharmacologic MD2/TLR4 perturbation.

context_scope: SAA3 peptide binding, TLR4/MD2 assays and MyD88/p38/NFkB readouts
exact_evidence_status: exact mouse SAA3-fragment-MD2/TLR4 complex edge; fragment boundary explicit
evidence_summary: Synthetic SAA3(20-86) and (43-57) peptides show direct SPR binding to purified TLR4/MD2 and MD2-dependent signaling; an independent premetastatic primary study assigns TLR4 as a functional receptor for SAA3.
limitations: Promoted only for the defined mouse SAA3 peptide/MD2-TLR4 edge; not full-length human SAA3; no SCI model; downstream p38/NFkB remains separate.

context_scope: VCAN perturbation, TLR2/TLR6/CD14 dependence and cytokine assays
exact_evidence_status: exact VCAN-TLR2:TLR6/CD14 complex edge; not a binary VCAN-TLR2 claim
evidence_summary: Primary biochemical and cell studies identify a TLR2/TLR6/CD14 complex for VCAN inflammatory activity; an independent 2025 primary study reproduces VCAN-TLR2-MyD88 inflammatory signaling.
limitations: Promoted at the complex level only; no purified binary VCAN-TLR2 binding, no SCI model, and downstream macrophage polarization remains distinct.

context_scope: CCR10-dependent chemotaxis and recruitment assays
cell_type_context: T-cell and skin homing comparator models
exact_evidence_status: exact CCL27-CCR10 chemokine-GPCR edge
evidence_summary: Primary chemotaxis and recruitment studies support CCL27-CCR10, independently reproduced by the original orphan-receptor binding report and newer receptor selectivity/structure-function work.
limitations: High confidence is molecular only; no SCI model; skin-homing context and chemokine glycosaminoglycan presentation remain separate from the exact receptor edge.

context_scope: CCR3-dependent migration/eosinophil response assays
exact_evidence_status: exact CCL28-CCR3 chemokine-GPCR edge; dual-receptor usage retained
evidence_summary: Primary CCL28-CCR3 comparator pharmacology is independently supported by receptor-selectivity and structural work distinguishing CCR3 from the shared CCR10 branch.
limitations: High confidence is the exact CCR3 edge, not exclusive receptor usage; CCL28-CCR10 remains separate; no SCI model.

context_scope: CCR1 affinity and signaling assays
exact_evidence_status: exact CCL7-CCR1 chemokine-GPCR edge
evidence_summary: Primary receptor pharmacology and a later two-site CCR1 binding/activation study identify CCL7 as a cognate CCR1 ligand; independent MCP chemokine work supports receptor-proximal signaling.
limitations: High confidence is molecular only; CCL7 is promiscuous across chemokine receptors and no SCI receptor-causal validation was located.

context_scope: CCR2B affinity, calcium and chemotaxis assays
exact_evidence_status: exact CCL7-CCR2B chemokine-GPCR edge
evidence_summary: Primary CCL7/MCP-3 receptor pharmacology plus independent MCP-3 chemotaxis and CCR2B-transfectant signaling studies support the exact CCR2B edge.
limitations: High confidence is molecular only; CCL7 is multi-receptor and no SCI receptor-causal validation was located; retain CCR1/CCR3 edges separately.

context_scope: CCR3 affinity/signaling and cellular response assays
cell_type_context: heterologous receptor and pain comparator systems
exact_evidence_status: exact CCL7-CCR3 chemokine-GPCR edge; receptor-proximal effect distinct from pain output
evidence_summary: Primary CCL7 receptor pharmacology and independent CCR3 antagonist experiments in trigeminal neurons support CCL7-CCR3 receptor-proximal signaling.
limitations: High confidence is molecular/receptor-proximal only; trigeminal pain and ERK are downstream; no SCI-specific receptor-causal validation and CCL7 also engages CCR2.

context_scope: extracellular CIRP challenge and TLR4/MD2 inflammatory assays
exact_evidence_status: exact extracellular CIRBP-CIRP-TLR4/MD2 complex edge with direct binding
evidence_summary: Primary SPR and mutational evidence maps extracellular CIRP residues 106-125 to MD2/TLR4 signaling; independent trauma and inflammatory studies reproduce TLR4-dependent CIRP effects.
limitations: High confidence is a TLR4/MD2 complex edge, not a generic binary TLR4 claim; no SCI model and no endogenous lesion-source experiment.

context_scope: mature peptide exposure and TLR4-dependent dendritic-cell maturation assays
exact_evidence_status: exact mature mouse DEFB2-TLR4 ligand-receptor edge
evidence_summary: Mature murine beta-defensin-2 directly acts as a TLR4 ligand in dendritic-cell assays; independent mouse studies reproduce TLR4/MyD88-dependent beta-defensin-2 responses.
limitations: Promoted only for mature mouse DEFB2; peptide and species identity matter; no SCI model and no claim about generic human beta-defensin or downstream outputs.

context_scope: selective B1 agonist/antagonist pharmacology
cell_type_context: rat detrusor, urothelium, DRG, and spinal cord
compartment_context: cell surface/bladder and spinal autonomic circuits
exact_evidence_status: exact des-Arg9-bradykinin-BDKRB1 pharmacologic edge
evidence_summary: Selective B1 agonist and antagonist experiments support a des-Arg9-bradykinin/BDKRB1 axis in rat SCI-associated bladder dysfunction; independent cloned-receptor pharmacology confirms des-Arg9-bradykinin activation of B1.
limitations: High confidence is pharmacologic; no purified binding or endogenous kallikrein cleavage/lesion-core ligand-source experiment.

context_scope: primary SCII bradykinin treatment, B2R, cytokine, p65, and neuronal-recovery assays
cell_type_context: rat injured spinal cord and neuronal compartment
exact_evidence_status: exact bradykinin-BDKRB2 pharmacologic edge
evidence_summary: Bradykinin treatment and B2R expression or blockade improve inflammatory and locomotor outcomes after spinal ischemia; independent rat preconditioning and intrathecal antagonist studies support B2R mediation.
limitations: High confidence is pharmacologic; no purified bradykinin-B2R binding and no lesion-core endogenous release experiment; recovery is downstream of the receptor edge.
